Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova, et amplissima collectio, in qua praeter ea quae Phil. Labbeus et Gabr. Cossartius S.J. et novissime Nicolaus Coleti in lucem edidere, ea omnia insuper suis in locis optime disposita exhibentur, quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi evulgavit. Tomus Quintus: ab anno CCCCXXXI ad annum CCCCXLI
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction for H. Welter, Paris and Leipzig, of the Florence edition 'expensis Antonii Zatta Veneti'
Publication Date: 1901 (the Welter facsimile; 'H. WELTER' at file line 101 and 'EXPENSIS ANTONII ZATTA VENETI' at 97; the facsimile's own dated imprint line is not legible in this OCR of this volume, but is legible in the tomus 6 and 7 scans of the same reprint vendored beside it; the original edition is catalogued by archive.org as 1761)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: the underlying edition is of 1761 and the facsimile of 1901); the item record carries no rights field
Language: lat (Latin, with the Greek of the conciliar texts printed in the original; the OCR renders the long s as f and recovers the Greek column only in part)
Source: archive.org item sacrorumconcilio0005joan (catalogue title 'SACRORUM CONCILIORUM', volume 5, catalogue date 1761, contributor Internet Archive), full text at https://archive.org/download/sacrorumconcilio0005joan/sacrorumconcilio0005joan_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-10-17 by the Shared-Events source-research thread (Era 2 worker D); the byte count of the downloaded file (4,248,174) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: an eighteenth-century edition in a 1901 facsimile is out of US copyright under this project's pd-us-by-date rule on either date. Same printing and same vendoring discipline as the tomus 2, 3 and 4 files already in this directory.
Content note: Mansi tomus 5, 431 to 441 (span at file line 85): the aftermath of the Council of Ephesus and the Antiochene dissent. The acts of the Antiochene counter-council ('Conciliabulum Ephesinum', index 325, heading 46711), the letters of John of Antioch (28921, and others), the reunion correspondence of 433, the letters of Celestine and Sixtus, and the SYNODICON ADVERSUS TRAGOEDIAM IRENAEI (index 360; heading 72980; its manuscript source noted at 73060), the Latin dossier of the Antiochene side built around Irenaeus of Tyre's lost Tragoedia. The volume's index of Leo's early letters includes Flavian's two letters to Leo (641, 655). The one vendored text that carries the Eastern bishops' dissent at Ephesus in documents rather than in narrative.
